page: Microsoft Azure E64pds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the 64-bit ARM architecture. Powered by Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processors operating at 3.4 GHz, the instance supplies 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, matching 64 vCPUs. The hardware configuration integrates 512.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB memory-to-core ratio, alongside 128 MB of shared L3 cache and 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core. In addition to compute and memory resources, the server includes 3,780 GB of attached local NVMe SSD storage. It operates without hardware GPU accelerators under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data reveals exceptional multi-threaded computational and memory subsystem throughput. The instance achieves top-tier results in multi-core tests, registering 132,397.85 in stress-ng and 23,580.0 in Geekbench multi-core, alongside top-tier Clang software compilation throughput. While single-core scores remain in the average tier, the server demonstrates outstanding memory bandwidth, measuring 465.82 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 203.93 GB/sec for writes. Database operations and static web serving throughput also reach top-tier percentiles, backed by strong Redis performance of 117.06 million SET operations per second.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the dedicated ARM core topology and high memory density yield competitive resource utilization for scale-out architectures. The presence of fast, high-capacity local NVMe storage reduces external disk latency and offloads I/O bottlenecks. Tradeoffs include average single-threaded compute output and the absence of x86 vector instruction sets like AVX-512. The instance is optimally matched for high-concurrency in-memory databases, large-scale caching layers, distributed data processing, and intensive multi-threaded compilation pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E64pds_v6 is a memory-optimized cloud server driven by a 64-core ARM Neoverse-N2 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz with dedicated single-threaded physical cores. The instance features 512.0 GB of RAM, offering an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, complemented by 128 MB of L3 cache and 3,780 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark results show top-tier multi-threaded compute performance and memory throughput, clocking 465.82 GB/sec uncached reads and exceptional database transaction rates, while single-core processing remains average. The server contains no GPU hardware and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. With balanced memory capacity and dedicated ARM cores, the instance provides strong resource efficiency for multi-threaded workloads, making it well suited for large in-memory caching layers, relational or NoSQL database management systems, data processing engines, and multi-core compilation tasks.
